fullDaySay: You push through the doors into open air. Haven grounds — tents, a fire pit, worn paths. The world is that way.

"Hey." A man, maybe 30s, with a limp settles near you, not too close. "Day one. Everyone's pretending they're fine. ...Can we talk? Just talk — like people used to." (Talk to A man, maybe 30s, with a limp.)
Recipe: Bark armor (Level 1). You have seen bark armor. Plates of bark laced together, worn like a shell.

🛡️ Dawn at Haven. By the fire hangs an old bark cuirass, split at the seam — somebody's grandfather wore this into the treeline and came back. The shape of it is clear: bark plates laced overlapping like shingles, vine cord. Your hands don't know it yet. Your eyes do.
⚠ STARVING: health and energy falling. You went to bed on an empty stomach.
Village meal: +1200 kcal, +1L water from the communal pantry. (Half ration — they don't trust you yet.)
Someone told a joke by the fire. You hear A woman, maybe 40s laugh — a real one.
A woman, maybe 30s is hurt — a fall, a thorn, a bad step. (health 84/100)

(Talking costs a little energy — 10 kcal a conversation. Small talk is cheap; going deep costs time, not more food.)

Travel 1 tile to forest floor.
— Under the canopy —
Saplings push up through last year's deadfall, racing each other for the light. The forest never stops trying.
Something big is moving in the woods. The birds went quiet.
You see smoke on the horizon. Stonebridge — 10 people, 3 days in. foragers, by the look of it. They know 4 plants — 4 new to you. They've been here the whole time.
You catch fragments by the fire — Adaeze telling A man, maybe 40s about you. The truth left this story two fires ago. What's left is better theater.
Journal: Deep shade. The floor keeps its secrets.
📓 Journal: you UNDERSTAND **Green Thumb, Literally**. It resonates with: something unnamed, something unnamed.
You work the patch with practiced hands: 5× Mayapple (350 kcal). This patch is picked clean — it'll recover in a few days.
Travel 1 tile to Haven.
You keep a day's food (350 kcal) — nothing extra for the pantry this time.
You walk back into Haven. 4 Codex entries. The village is glad to see you.
You sow Mayapple: 180 days to first harvest. Later harvests need 45 days of regrowth. Tend daily; garden magic can accelerate growth. (2 units sown.)

Fireside lesson: Daniyar passes around a climbing vine with alien-looking purple-and-white flowers and wrinkled purple-yellow fruit. Someone asks a dumb question. Nobody minds. That's how you learn.
★ IDENTIFIED: Maracujá (Passion Fruit). Maracujá. Wrinkled fruit, incredible smell, scoop the inside. Uses unknown — harvest, taste, and learn.

Fresh-cut stems on the northwest ground — someone else is working turf your crews use. (Stonebridge's foragers, most likely. You walk the ground yourself: it's thinner than your crews alone could strip it.)
You've started noticing: A man, maybe 50s, with a gap-toothed grin and Ezra never speak. It's not new. (Something old lives in Haven.)
— DAY 4 DAWN — The world wakes. Animals are active.
The fire burns low. One new line in the journal: Maracujá (Passion Fruit) — named and noted.
👀 Hank claims to belong somewhere — then spends the whole evening oriented around something they won't name. The wanting is real. The word for it isn't "to belong somewhere".

You catch fragments by the fire — A man, maybe 20s telling A woman, maybe 40s about herself. The retelling is already better than the event.
You catch fragments by the fire — Olivia telling Hank about A man, maybe 20s. The story's getting bigger than what happened.

Travel 2 tiles to forest floor.
— Under the canopy —
Old growth. The canopy closes overhead and the light comes down in shafts. Something rustled, and decided not to be seen.
It followed you. Something displaced a LOT of water is here.

👁 Never grab it barehanded. A bow works clean; hands get quills. Flip it with a long stick if you must.

While you were gone — one thing you missed:

Someone by the fire nods at the counter. "We pool food here. Keep what you need for the road — the rest feeds everyone, once it's food."
Nobody at the fire knows your haul any better than you do. It'll be your own hands that teach you.

💡 You see it again in your mind: a tree with lobed leaves and oval nuts in scaly caps. your teacher's words land on the memory like a label. White Oak Acorns. Of course.
Miguel was watching. Now they know White Oak Acorns too.

It will release to protect them. On land it is slow and heavy; it needs the water to be the Empress. Never let it get a second wrap. (Two survived encounters — the fire has a theory.)
